memoize.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement memoize(fn)
memoize.what:
Implement memoize(fn) that returns a memoized version of fn. It should cache results by arguments. Support an optional resolver function to compute the cache key. Add a .cache property and .clear() method.

Requirements

  • Cache result keyed by JSON.stringify(args) by default
  • Support optional resolver(args) to compute custom cache key
  • Expose .cache Map on the returned function
  • Add .clear() method to wipe the cache
  • Handle functions with object arguments (key serialisation)

Concepts: closures · Map · JSON.stringify · higher-order functions
memoize.why:
• Store a Map inside the closure. Key = resolver ? resolver(...args) : JSON.stringify(args). Check map before calling fn.
  • JSON.stringify has limitations with undefined, Symbol, circular refs. Mention this as a tradeoff.

throttle.desc: Limits how often a function fires. The sibling of debounce — often confused with it.
throttle.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement throttle(fn, delay)
throttle.what:
Implement throttle(fn, delay). The returned function should invoke fn at most once every delay ms, regardless of how many times it's called. Support both leading and trailing calls.

Requirements

  • Basic throttle — invoke at most once per delay window
  • Leading call fires immediately on first invocation
  • Trailing call: if called during the window, fire once the window ends
  • Returns wrapper with same args as fn
  • Cancel method to clear pending trailing call

Concepts: closures · timers · rate limiting · higher-order functions
throttle.why:
• Track a lastCalled timestamp. On each invocation, check if (now - lastCalled) >= delay. If yes, call fn and update lastCalled.
  • For trailing: store the last args in the closure and use setTimeout to invoke fn after the remaining window.

debounce.desc: A classic — every interviewer loves this. Delay execution until the user stops firing.
debounce.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement debounce(fn, delay)
debounce.what:
Implement a debounce(fn, delay) function. The returned function should only invoke fn after delay milliseconds have elapsed since the last call. Also add a .cancel() method to cancel any pending invocation.

Requirements

  • Basic debounce — delay execution after quiet period
  • Returns a wrapper function with same args as fn
  • Add .cancel() method to cancel pending timer
  • Handle this context correctly inside fn
  • Leading edge option: fire immediately on first call if { leading: true } passed

Concepts: closures · timers · higher-order functions · this binding
debounce.why:
• Use setTimeout and clearTimeout. Store the timer ID in a variable the closure can access.
  • For leading edge: invoke fn immediately if no timer is currently running, then set the timer to reset the "can fire" state.

curry.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement curry(fn)
curry.what:
Write curry(fn) that returns a curried version of fn. The curried function should accept arguments one at a time and invoke fn only when all arguments have been collected. It should also support partial application (passing multiple args at once).

Requirements

  • Works for functions of any arity (fn.length)
  • Supports passing args one at a time: add(1)(2)(3)
  • Supports partial application: add(1,2)(3)
  • Returns the result when all args are collected
  • Handle functions with default params (fn.length caveat)

Concepts: closures · recursion · function.length · partial application

pipe-compose.desc: Function composition — the backbone of functional programming in JS.
pipe-compose.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement pipe() and compose()
pipe-compose.why:
• pipe = (...fns) => x => fns.reduce((v, f) => f(v), x). Compose is the same but with reduceRight.
  • pipeAsync: use fns.reduce((promise, fn) => promise.then(fn), Promise.resolve(x))

flatten.q: How will you solve this problem? Flatten Nested Array
flatten.what:
Implement flatten(arr, depth = Infinity) that works like Array.prototype.flat(). Flatten nested arrays up to the given depth. Also implement a version using a stack (iterative) for bonus points.

Requirements

  • Handles any level of nesting
  • Respects depth parameter (flatten(arr, 1) only one level)
  • Does not modify the original array
  • Works with mixed types (numbers, strings, nested arrays)
  • Iterative stack-based solution as a bonus

Concepts: recursion · Array.isArray · spread operator · stack

deep-clone.q: How will you solve this problem? Deep Clone an Object
deep-clone.why:
• Use a WeakMap to track already-visited objects. Before cloning an object, check if it's in the map. If yes, return the cloned version from the map.
  • Check type in order: null → array → Date → RegExp → Map → Set → plain object.

once.desc: Execute a function exactly once. Return the same value on subsequent calls.
once.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement once(fn)
once.what:
Implement once(fn) that returns a wrapper which invokes fn at most once. On all subsequent calls, return the result of the first invocation without calling fn again.

Requirements

  • fn called only on first invocation
  • Subsequent calls return the same cached result
  • Preserves fn's this context on first call
  • Works with any number of arguments
  • Clear internal state via a .reset() method (bonus)

Concepts: closures · flag variables · this binding
once.why:
• Use a boolean flag and a cached result variable in the closure.
  • let called = false, result; return function(...args){ if(!called){ called=true; result=fn.apply(this,args); } return result; }
  • For .reset(): set called=false and result=undefined. This allows fn to be invoked again on the next call.

groupby.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement groupBy(array, key)
groupby.why: • Use reduce with {} as accumulator. Compute the key with typeof key === "function" ? key(item) : item[key]. Push item into acc[k] = acc[k] || [];

array-methods.desc: Can you recreate the Array prototype methods? Tests your understanding of callbacks and accumulators.
array-methods.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement map / filter / reduce from Scratch
array-methods.what:
Implement myMap(arr, fn), myFilter(arr, fn), and myReduce(arr, fn, initialValue) without using the built-in methods. Each should match the native behaviour including edge cases.

Requirements

  • myMap: applies fn(item, index, array) to each element
  • myFilter: returns new array with elements where fn returns truthy
  • myReduce: when no initialValue, use first element as accumulator
  • All three pass index and original array to callback
  • Throw TypeError for non-function callback (matches native)

Concepts: callbacks · accumulators · array iteration · prototype methods

bind.desc: The mother of all polyfills — tests this binding, partial application, and the new operator trap.
bind.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Function.prototype.bind
bind.what:
Implement Function.prototype.bind(thisArg, ...partials). It returns a new function with this set to thisArg and prepends partials to args. The tricky part: when used with new, the this value is ignored — the new instance takes precedence.

Requirements

  • Returns a new function that calls original with fixed this
  • Supports partial application: bind(ctx, a, b)(c, d) → fn.call(ctx, a, b, c, d)
  • When used as constructor (new), the bound this is ignored
  • Bound function's prototype is preserved for instanceof checks
  • Handle missing thisArg (default to globalThis)

Concepts: this binding · partial application · new operator · prototype chain
bind.why:
• Store fn and thisArg in closure. Return a wrapper that merges boundArgs + callArgs.
  • For the new trap: check if called with new via instanceof. If so, return new original(...mergedArgs) — not fn.apply(thisArg, mergedArgs).

object-assign.desc: Merging objects is everywhere — implement the spec correctly including getter invocation.
object-assign.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Object.assign
object-assign.what:
Implement Object.assign(target, ...sources). Copy own enumerable string-keyed properties from sources to target using [[Get]] on source and [[Set]] on target. Return target.

Requirements

  • Copies own enumerable string-keyed properties only (no Symbol keys)
  • Uses [[Get]] on source (invokes getters) and [[Set]] on target
  • Later sources overwrite earlier ones
  • Null/undefined sources are skipped (no error)
  • Primitive sources are coerced to objects
  • Returns the modified target object

Concepts: Object.keys · property descriptors · for...in vs own properties
object-assign.why:
• Loop sources with forEach. For each, get Object.keys(source) and for each key do target[key] = source[key].
  • The subtlety: using source[key] invokes getters, which is spec-correct. Do NOT use getOwnPropertyDescriptor + getter.

array-from.desc: The most versatile Array static — handle iterables, array-likes, and a map function.
array-from.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Array.from

array-find.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Array.prototype.find
array-find.what:
Implement Array.prototype.find(callback, thisArg?). Returns the first element satisfying the callback. If none matches, return undefined. Handle sparse arrays correctly.

Requirements

  • Returns first element where callback returns truthy
  • Returns undefined if no element matches
  • callback receives (element, index, array)
  • Optional thisArg sets this in callback
  • Skips empty slots in sparse arrays
  • Does not mutate the original array

Concepts: array iteration · early termination · sparse arrays · this binding

array-includes.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Array.prototype.includes

string-methods.desc: Three string methods with subtle spec details — position handling and the RegExp guard.
string-methods.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement String.prototype.startsWith / endsWith / includes
string-methods.why:
• startsWith: position = Math.min(Math.max(pos, 0), this.length). Slice from position to position+len, compare.
  • The RegExp guard: if (searchString instanceof RegExp) throw new TypeError(). This is a spec requirement.

object-create.desc: The foundation of ES5 prototypal inheritance — set up [[Prototype]] without the built-in.
object-create.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Object.create
object-create.what:
Implement Object.create(proto, propertiesObject?). Creates a new object with [[Prototype]] set to proto. The optional second argument adds property descriptors (like Object.defineProperties).

Requirements

  • Returns new object with [[Prototype]] set to proto
  • If proto is null, create a null-prototype object
  • If proto is not object and not null, throw TypeError
  • Optional propertiesObject defines own properties via Object.defineProperties
  • Used for: Child.prototype = Object.create(Parent.prototype)
  • Handle proto === null (no prototype chain)

Concepts: prototypal inheritance · Object.defineProperties · null prototype · constructor
object-create.why:
• Temporary constructor trick: function F(){}; F.prototype = proto; return new F(). Works for any proto except null.
  • For null: use Object.setPrototypeOf({}, null) or the temp constructor approach with Object.create(null) fallback.

some-every.desc: The logical quantifiers — early-terminating iteration with vacuous truth semantics.
some-every.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Array.prototype.some and every

array-map.desc: The most-used array method — implement the full spec including sparse array handling and thisArg.
array-map.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Array.prototype.map
array-map.what:
Implement Array.prototype.map(callback, thisArg?) on the Array prototype. It creates a new array populated with the results of calling callback on every element. Handle sparse arrays correctly — empty slots should remain empty in the result.

Requirements

  • Returns a new array (does not mutate original)
  • callback receives (element, index, array)
  • Optional thisArg sets this inside callback
  • Skips empty slots in sparse arrays (does not call callback, slot stays empty)
  • Throws TypeError if callback is not a function
  • Works on array-like objects (not just Array instances)

Concepts: prototype methods · array iteration · sparse arrays · this binding
array-map.why:
• Use a standard for loop. Check i in array to handle sparse arrays. For each present slot: result[i] = callback.call(thisArg, array[i], i, array).
  • The key spec detail: map creates a hole in the output for every hole in the input — it does not fill sparse slots with undefined.

array-filter.desc: Understanding sparse arrays in filter is the real test — holes are always skipped.
array-filter.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Array.prototype.filter
array-filter.what:
Implement Array.prototype.filter(callback, thisArg?). Returns a new array with only the elements where callback returns truthy. Unlike map, filter naturally compacts sparse arrays — it never produces holes.

Requirements

  • Returns a new array (does not mutate original)
  • callback receives (element, index, array)
  • Optional thisArg sets this in callback
  • Skips empty slots in sparse arrays
  • Throws TypeError if callback is not a function
  • Result array is always dense (no holes) — elements are shifted left

Concepts: prototype methods · array iteration · sparse arrays · truthiness
array-filter.why:
• Loop with i in array check. If callback returns truthy, push to result. Since push() appends sequentially, the result is always dense.
  • The sparse-to-dense behaviour is unique to filter — map preserves holes, filter removes them.

array-reduce.desc: The most subtle of the trio — handling missing initialValue on an empty array is the trap.
array-reduce.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Array.prototype.reduce
array-reduce.what:
Implement Array.prototype.reduce(callback, initialValue?). Executes a reducer function on each element, resulting in a single output value. If no initialValue, use the first element as the accumulator and start from index 1.

Requirements

  • callback receives (accumulator, element, index, array)
  • If initialValue is provided, acc = initialValue, loop from index 0
  • If no initialValue, acc = first element, loop from index 1
  • Throws TypeError on empty array with no initialValue
  • Throws TypeError if callback is not a function
  • Skips empty slots in sparse arrays (does not count them)

Concepts: accumulators · edge cases · sparse arrays · TypeError
array-reduce.why:
• Check if initialValue === undefined (not just falsy — 0 and "" are valid initial values). Use arguments.length < 2 to detect missing initialValue.
  • For no initialValue: find the first non-sparse index. If none found (empty array), throw TypeError. Use that as initial acc, start loop from index+1.

array-flat-flatmap.desc: flatten and map-then-flatten — flatMap is the union of map and flat(1), asked heavily at product companies.
array-flat-flatmap.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Array.prototype.flat and flatMap
array-flat-flatmap.what:
Implement Array.prototype.flat(depth = 1) and Array.prototype.flatMap(callback, thisArg?). flat recursively flattens nested arrays up to depth. flatMap is identical to map().flat(1) but only flattens one level.

Requirements

  • flat(depth): recursively flatten nested arrays up to given depth (default 1)
  • flat(Infinity) flattens completely
  • flat removes empty slots in the flattened result
  • flatMap: maps each element then flattens result by one level
  • flatMap is NOT map + flat(1) in one pass — it avoids creating the intermediate array
  • Both return new arrays, never mutate original

Concepts: recursion · flattening · prototype methods · flatMap as map + flatten
array-flat-flatmap.why:
• flat: iterate with for loop. If element is array and depth > 0, recurse with depth-1 and push each result. Otherwise push element directly. Holes are naturally dropped.
  • flatMap: call callback on each element. The callback should return an array. Use result.push(...callback(item, i, arr)) to flatten one level. Equivalent to [].concat(...arr.map(callback)).

call-apply.desc: The foundation of explicit this binding — implement the methods that bind, call, and apply are built upon.
call-apply.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Function.prototype.call and apply
call-apply.what:
Implement Function.prototype.call(thisArg, ...args) and Function.prototype.apply(thisArg, argsArray). Both invoke the function with a specific this value. call takes arguments individually, apply takes an array. Handle edge cases: null/undefined thisArg defaults to globalThis, non-function callers throw TypeError.

Requirements

  • call: invokes function with thisArg and individual args
  • apply: invokes function with thisArg and args as an array
  • null/undefined thisArg → default to globalThis (window/global)
  • Throw TypeError if caller is not a function
  • apply: if argsArray is null/undefined, treat as empty array
  • Handle primitives as thisArg (coerce via Object())

Concepts: this binding · globalThis · function methods · type checking

string-trim.desc: Seems trivial — but the spec defines whitespace broadly and you need to handle both ends.
string-trim.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement String.prototype.trim
string-trim.what:
Implement String.prototype.trim(), trimStart(), and trimEnd(). Remove whitespace from both ends (trim), the start (trimStart), or the end (trimEnd). Whitespace includes: space, tab, no-break space, line terminators (\n, \r, \f, \v), and all Unicode whitespace.

Requirements

  • trim(): removes whitespace from both ends
  • trimStart(): removes whitespace from the start only
  • trimEnd(): removes whitespace from the end only
  • Define whitespace: space, tab, no-break space, line terminators
  • If string is all whitespace, return empty string
  • Does not mutate the original string (strings are immutable)

Concepts: string methods · whitespace definition · regular expressions · immutability

array-sort.desc: The most complex Array prototype method — implement the default string sort and comparator support.
array-sort.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Array.prototype.sort (basic)
array-sort.what:
Implement Array.prototype.sort(compareFn?). The default sort converts elements to strings and compares UTF-16 code units. If compareFn is provided, sort uses it: negative means a < b, positive means a > b, zero means equal. Return the same array (sorted in-place).

Requirements

  • Default sort: converts elements to strings, compares by UTF-16 code unit values
  • compareFn: (a, b) => negative (a first), positive (b first), zero (stable order)
  • Sorts in-place and returns the modified array
  • Handles sparse arrays (empty slots are moved to the end)
  • Stable sort: equal elements maintain original relative order
  • Throws TypeError if compareFn is not a function (when provided)

Concepts: comparators · in-place sorting · string coercion · stable sort · sparse arrays
array-sort.why:
• Implement a simple stable sort like insertion sort or merge sort. Insertion sort is O(n²) but stable and in-place: for i=1..n-1, insert arr[i] into sorted portion [0..i-1].
  • Default comparator: (a, b) => String(a) < String(b) ? -1 : String(a) > String(b) ? 1 : 0. Sparse slots: track holes and append them at the end.

promise-static.desc: The simplest Promise static methods — but the thenable unwrapping in resolve is the hidden detail.
promise-static.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Promise.resolve and Promise.reject
promise-static.what:
Implement Promise.resolve(value) and Promise.reject(reason). resolve returns a Promise resolved with the value (unwrapping thenables). reject returns a Promise rejected with the reason.

Requirements

  • Promise.resolve(value): returns a fulfilled Promise with value
  • If value is a Promise, return it as-is (no wrapping)
  • If value is a thenable (has .then method), unwrap it by calling value.then(resolve, reject)
  • Promise.reject(reason): returns a rejected Promise with reason
  • reject does NOT unwrap thenables — wraps them as-is
  • Both are static methods on Promise (not on instances)

Concepts: Promise · thenable detection · static methods · unwrap semantics

reduce-right.desc: Like reduce but from the right — the symmetry reveals whether you truly understand the accumulator pattern.
reduce-right.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Array.prototype.reduceRight
reduce-right.what:
Implement Array.prototype.reduceRight(callback, initialValue?). Same as reduce but iterates from right to left (last element to first). If no initialValue, the last element is used as accumulator and iteration starts from second-last.

Requirements

  • Iterates from rightmost to leftmost element
  • callback receives (accumulator, element, index, array)
  • If initialValue provided, acc = initialValue, loop from last index to 0
  • If no initialValue, acc = last element, loop from length-2 to 0
  • Throws TypeError on empty array with no initialValue
  • Skips empty slots in sparse arrays

Concepts: accumulator pattern · right-to-left iteration · sparse arrays · TypeError
reduce-right.why:
• Same logic as reduce but the loop goes backward: for (let i = len-1; i >= 0; i--). Check i in array for sparse support.
  • For no initialValue: find the last non-sparse index from the end. Use that as acc, start loop from i-1 going backward.

eventemitter.desc: The backbone of Node.js. Building it from scratch is a top-5 machine coding question.
eventemitter.q: How will you solve this problem? Build EventEmitter (on/off/emit/once)
eventemitter.why:
• Store listeners in a Map: event → Set of listeners. For once, wrap the listener in a function that calls off then the original.
  • For off: Map.get(event)?.delete(listener). For once: wrap as a oneTime fn, call on(event, oneTime), inside oneTime call off(event, oneTime) then listener(...args).

lru.desc: Get and put in O(1). The classic data structure question dressed as machine coding.
lru.q: How will you solve this problem? LRU Cache — O(1) get & put
lru.what:
Implement an LRUCache(capacity) class with get(key) returning the value or -1, and put(key, value) inserting/updating and evicting the least-recently-used item when capacity is exceeded.

Requirements

  • get(key): O(1) — return value or -1 if not found, mark as recently used
  • put(key, value): O(1) — insert or update, evict LRU if over capacity
  • Both operations count as "use" (update recency)
  • Handle capacity = 1 edge case
  • Bonus: implement as a doubly linked list + Map (show the internals)

Concepts: Map (insertion-order) · doubly linked list · O(1) operations · hash map
lru.why:
• Use a Map — it preserves insertion order. To mark as recently used: delete(key) then set(key, value). To evict LRU: map.keys().next().value gives the oldest.
  • For the DLL approach: Map stores key → node. DLL maintains order. On access: remove node from DLL and move to head. On eviction: remove tail.

promise-scratch.desc: The deepest internals question. Shows you truly understand async JavaScript.
promise-scratch.q: How will you solve this problem? Build Promise from Scratch

promise-combinators.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Promise.all / race / allSettled / any
promise-combinators.what:
Implement Promise.all(promises), Promise.race(promises), Promise.allSettled(promises), and Promise.any(promises) from scratch using only the base Promise constructor.

Requirements

  • all: resolves with array of values; rejects on first rejection
  • race: settles with the first promise to settle
  • allSettled: always resolves with array of {status, value|reason}
  • any: resolves with first fulfilled; rejects with AggregateError if all reject
  • All handle empty arrays correctly
  • Preserve result order regardless of resolution order (for .all)

Concepts: Promise · counter pattern · AggregateError · async coordination

concurrency-limiter.q: How will you solve this problem? Async Concurrency Limiter
concurrency-limiter.what:
Implement runWithConcurrency(tasks, limit) where tasks is an array of functions returning Promises. Run at most limit tasks simultaneously. Return a Promise that resolves with all results in original order.

Requirements

  • Maximum limit tasks running at any time
  • Results array preserves original task order
  • Starts next task as soon as any running task completes
  • Returns Promise resolving with all results
  • Handle task rejections (reject the outer Promise)

Concepts: Promise · queue · async/await · generators
concurrency-limiter.why:
• Keep an index into the tasks array. Start limit tasks initially. When any task completes, start the next one from the queue. Use Promise.race or a "worker" pattern.
  • Worker pattern: create limit worker Promises. Each worker pulls from the queue and awaits, then pulls again, until queue is empty. Use Promise.all(workers).

deep-equal.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement deepEqual(a, b)

retry.q: How will you solve this problem? Retry with Exponential Backoff
retry.what:
Implement retry(fn, retries, delay). Call async fn. If it rejects, wait delay ms then retry. Double the delay each attempt (exponential backoff). After retries attempts, reject with the last error. Support a shouldRetry(error) predicate.

Requirements

  • Retry up to retries times on failure
  • Exponential backoff: delay doubles each attempt (delay * 2^attempt)
  • Optional shouldRetry(err): if returns false, stop retrying immediately
  • Resolve with fn's return value on success
  • Reject with last error after all retries exhausted

Concepts: async/await · recursion · exponential backoff · error handling
retry.why:
• Use a recursive async function with attempt counter. Catch the error, check shouldRetry, then await a sleep(delay * 2**attempt) before recursing.
  • sleep = ms => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms))

chainable.q: How will you solve this problem? Build a Chainable Query Builder
chainable.why:
• Store an array of {method, fn} objects. value() runs them in sequence using the appropriate array method.
  • Return this from each method. Store operations as {type:"filter", fn} and reduce over them in value().

promise-timeout.q: How will you solve this problem? Implement Promise.withTimeout / Promise with Timeout
promise-timeout.what:
Implement withTimeout(promise, ms, fallback) that returns a new Promise which rejects with a TimeoutError (or resolves with a fallback) if the input promise does not settle within ms milliseconds. Build it on Promise.race. Also implement a sleep(ms) helper.

Requirements

  • withTimeout(p, ms) rejects with a TimeoutError if p is slower than ms
  • If p settles first, its result/error passes through unchanged
  • Must not leak: the losing race branch is observed so no unhandled rejection
  • Support a fallback value (or function) used instead of rejecting on timeout
  • Timer is cleared once the promise settles (no dangling timers)
  • sleep(ms) helper built on setTimeout

Concepts: Promise.race · setTimeout · timeout · unhandled rejection prevention
promise-timeout.why:
• withTimeout = (p, ms, fb) => Promise.race([p, sleep(ms).then(() => fb instanceof Function ? fb() : fb)]) - race the input against a timer that resolves to the fallback.
  • To avoid unhandled rejections on the losing branch, attach a noop .catch(() => {}) to both promises before racing.

circuit-breaker.desc: The resilience pattern Atlassian and every backend service uses - fail fast instead of hanging on a dead dependency.
circuit-breaker.q: How will you solve this problem? Circuit Breaker (Fail Fast)
circuit-breaker.why:
• Store {state, failures, cooldownUntil}. On error in CLOSED: increment failures; if it reaches the threshold, set OPEN and record cooldownUntil = now + cooldownPeriod.
  • While HALF_OPEN, allow at most probeCount in-flight calls. A success resets failures and returns to CLOSED; any failure reopens for another cooldown.

stopwatch.desc: Timing, intervals, and accuracy - the flip side of the countdown timer.
stopwatch.q: How will you solve this problem? Stopwatch with Lap Times
stopwatch.what:
Implement a Stopwatch class with: start(), pause(), reset(), lap(), getElapsed(), and getLaps(). Track elapsed time accurately with no drift when pausing and resuming. Expose a tick(cb) subscription for UI updates.

Requirements

  • start(): begins timing; no-op if already running
  • pause(): stops the clock; resume preserves accumulated time (no drift)
  • reset(): zeroes elapsed time and clears laps
  • lap(): records the split time since the previous lap
  • getElapsed(): total ms since start minus paused time
  • Accuracy: use Date.now() deltas, never a counter incremented by setInterval
  • tick(cb): calls cb(ms) periodically and returns an unsubscribe function

Concepts: Date.now() · setInterval · state machine · observer pattern
stopwatch.why:
• Track running, startTime, accumulatedMs. On pause: accumulatedMs += now - startTime. On resume: startTime = now. elapsed = accumulatedMs + (running ? now - startTime : 0).
  • tick() runs a setInterval that calls cb(getElapsed()). For laps, snapshot {lapMs, totalMs} using the same elapsed math.

consistent-hashing.desc: The technique behind Redis Cluster, DynamoDB, and every distributed cache - machine coding loves the ring.
consistent-hashing.q: How will you solve this problem? Consistent Hashing Ring
consistent-hashing.what:
Implement ConsistentHashing: a hash ring with N virtual nodes per server. Methods: addServer(name), removeServer(name), getServer(key). Adding or removing a server should only remap a small fraction of keys (about 1/N). Base the hash on crypto md5/sha1.

Requirements

  • addServer(name): places vNodes virtual node markers on the ring (default 150)
  • removeServer(name): removes all of its virtual node markers
  • getServer(key): find the first clockwise marker and map it back to its server
  • Adding/removing one server moves roughly 1/N of keys (verify by counting remapped keys)
  • Empty ring: throw or return null (documented behaviour)
  • serverStats(): per-server ownership counts for the current keys
  • getServer is deterministic for the same key

Concepts: hash ring · virtual nodes · SHA-1 · binary search · distributed systems
consistent-hashing.why:
• Ring = sorted array of hashes plus Map. getServer: hash the key, binary search for the first hash >= keyHash, wrap to index 0 if past the end.
  • Virtual nodes: for i in range(vNodes), hash(server + ":" + i) and place a marker pointing at server. More vNodes = smoother distribution but more memory.

mini-redux.desc: Implement the entire Redux API from scratch — the ultimate JS architecture question.
mini-redux.q: How will you solve this problem? Build mini-Redux (createStore)

reactive.desc: Build auto-tracking reactivity — the core mechanism behind Vue 3 and MobX.
reactive.q: How will you solve this problem? Reactive Data System (Vue-like)

virtual-dom.desc: The engine inside React, Vue, and every modern framework. Build the core yourself.
virtual-dom.q: How will you solve this problem? Minimal Virtual DOM + Diff

observable.desc: The foundation of RxJS — teach yourself reactive streams.
observable.q: How will you solve this problem? Build an Observable from Scratch
observable.why:
• Store the subscriber function. subscribe() creates an observer wrapper that checks "active" flag. Operators: return new Observable(observer => this.subscribe({next: v => fn(v) and pass to observer})).
  • take(n): wrap observer, count emissions, call unsubscribe() when count reaches n.

scheduler.q: How will you solve this problem? Priority Task Scheduler

di-container.q: How will you solve this problem? Dependency Injection Container
di-container.what:
Build a Container class with: register(name, factory), singleton(name, factory), resolve(name). Factory functions receive the container so they can resolve their own dependencies. Detect circular dependencies.

Requirements

  • register: creates a new instance every time it's resolved
  • singleton: creates instance once, caches it
  • resolve: calls factory with container, returns instance
  • Detect circular dependencies and throw descriptive error
  • Support resolving by class (auto-detect constructor name) as bonus

Concepts: closures · Map · circular dependency detection · factory pattern

analytics-sdk.desc: The exact question Google and Atlassian ask - batching, retries, offline queueing, and session tracking.
analytics-sdk.q: How would you solve this problem? Analytics SDK (batching, retry, session)
analytics-sdk.why:
• Keep events[] in memory. flush() copies and empties the queue, then sends. On failure, re-enqueue with a retry count and schedule a later flush.
  • Persist the whole queue as JSON on every track() (debounced). On init, load it back and flush after a short delay to recover offline events.

feature-flags.desc: Every product company ships with flags - build the SDK: rules, targeting, and deterministic bucketing.
feature-flags.q: How will you solve this problem? Feature Flag / A-B Test SDK
feature-flags.what:
Build a FeatureFlagClient. Flags are defined as {key, value, rules[]}. getFlag(key, user) evaluates rules in order and returns the value of the first match. Support percentage rollouts (deterministic by userId hash), allowlist targeting, and conditions on user properties.

Requirements

  • getFlag(key, user): evaluates rules in order, returns value of first matching rule
  • Default value returned when the flag is missing or no rule matches
  • Percentage rollout: hash(userId + key) % 100 < percent decides the bucket
  • Targeting: allowlist of userIds and segment matching on user properties
  • Rule operators: eq, in, contains, gt, lt on user properties
  • Local overrides map for QA (overrides all rules)
  • onEval callback fired per evaluation for analytics

Concepts: rules engine · deterministic hashing · user bucketing · rollout
feature-flags.why:
• hash(str): FNV-1a or djb2 returning 0-99. bucket = hash(userId + ":" + key). Rollout matches when bucket < rule.percentage.
  • Rule shape: {conditions: [{field, op, value}], percentage: 100, value}. Every condition must match AND the bucket must fall inside the percentage.

responsive-layout.q: How will you solve this problem? Responsive Dashboard Layout (CSS Grid)
responsive-layout.what:
Build a responsive dashboard layout with only HTML and CSS (no frameworks): a header, sidebar, main content area, and footer. Desktop: fixed sidebar beside a content grid. Tablet: sidebar collapses to icons. Mobile: single column with a toggleable menu. Use CSS Grid for the shell and Flexbox for alignment.

Requirements

  • Header spans the full width at the top
  • Sidebar fixed on desktop (min 220px), collapses to icons at 1024px, hidden behind a toggle at 768px
  • Main area uses CSS Grid for a card gallery that reflows 1 -> 2 -> 3 columns
  • Footer at the bottom
  • Sticky header and sidebar (no scroll jump)
  • Layout works without JS; JS only drives the mobile menu toggle

Concepts: CSS Grid · Flexbox · media queries · sticky positioning
responsive-layout.why:
• Shell: display:grid; grid-template-columns: 220px 1fr; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto. Below 768px switch to one column and overlay the sidebar.
  • Card gallery: grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr)) - it reflows automatically with no media queries.

navbar-vanilla.desc: The most common CSS widget — a navbar that collapses to a hamburger menu on mobile, no framework.
navbar-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Responsive Navbar (CSS + hamburger)
navbar-vanilla.what:
Build a responsive navbar with pure HTML/CSS and a tiny bit of vanilla JS: a logo, links on the right, active-link highlighting. Below 768px the links collapse behind a hamburger button that toggles an open/close menu. Only the toggle uses JS.

Requirements

  • Logo left, nav links right on desktop
  • Active link styled distinctly (aria-current="page")
  • Below 768px: links hidden, hamburger button shown
  • Clicking hamburger toggles the mobile menu open/closed
  • Clicking a link closes the mobile menu
  • Close on Escape key (bonus)
  • No framework — pure CSS + a class toggle

Concepts: CSS Flexbox · media queries · classList toggle · aria-expanded
navbar-vanilla.why:
• Hamburger = a button with 3 spans or an inline SVG. Rotate/translate the bars into an X when open.
  • Use aria-expanded on the button and aria-controls pointing at the menu. Escape key handler: document.addEventListener("keydown", ...).

toggle-css.q: How will you solve this problem? Custom Toggle Switch (pure CSS)
toggle-css.why:
• Wrap the input and a span: input + span. Hide the input (position:absolute; opacity:0) but keep it focusable.
  • input:checked + span: switch the background and translateX() the knob. input:disabled + span: reduce opacity.

tooltip-css.desc: A pure-CSS tooltip that stays on-screen near the edges — tests positioning thinking.
tooltip-css.q: How will you solve this problem? Tooltip with Edge Positioning
tooltip-css.what:
Build a tooltip system that appears on hover/focus of an element. Pure CSS positioning (top/bottom/left/right with an arrow), but it must clamp: a tooltip near the viewport edge must not overflow off-screen. Use data-tooltip="..." attributes so it's usable on any element.

Requirements

  • Tooltip shows on hover and on keyboard focus
  • Positions above the target by default, with data-position overrides (top/bottom/left/right)
  • Near the right/bottom viewport edge, the tooltip clamps back inside the viewport
  • Arrow pointing at the target
  • Small fade/slide-in transition
  • Uses data-tooltip attributes — no per-element JS

Concepts: position: absolute · viewport clamping · data attributes · :hover / :focus-visible
tooltip-css.why:
• Pure CSS can't know the viewport — position with transform and keep max-width; for true clamping use JS to measure getBoundingClientRect() and flip.
  • A minimal JS enhancer (document.querySelectorAll("[data-tooltip]")) can read position and flip a class when the rect overflows.

todo-vanilla.desc: The classic widget built with zero framework — DOM APIs and event delegation under pressure.
todo-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Todo App (vanilla DOM + localStorage)
todo-vanilla.what:
Build a Todo App with pure HTML/CSS/JS (no framework): add a todo on Enter, toggle complete, delete, filter All/Active/Completed, show the active count, and persist to localStorage. Edit a todo inline on double-click.

Requirements

  • Add todo on Enter key
  • Toggle individual todo complete
  • Delete individual todo
  • Filter tabs: All / Active / Completed
  • Show "X items left" count
  • Persist todos to localStorage (survive reload)
  • Inline edit on double-click (Enter or blur to save)

Concepts: event delegation · localStorage · data-* attributes · DOM creation
todo-vanilla.why:
• Rendering approach: one render() function that rebuilds the list from state (state -> DOM). Or DOM-diff with createElement/appendChild.
  • Event delegation: one click listener on the list container, read data-action + data-id from e.target.closest("[data-action]"). localStorage: JSON.stringify the state array on every change.

accordion-vanilla.desc: Event delegation and single/multi-open modes — the same widget as the React round, but no React.
accordion-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Accordion (vanilla)
accordion-vanilla.what:
Build an Accordion with vanilla JS: items rendered from an array [{id, title, content}], two modes (single — one panel open; multiple — several open), smooth max-height transition, and a chevron that rotates. No framework.

Requirements

  • Render items from a config array
  • single mode: opening one closes the others
  • multiple mode: panels toggle independently
  • Smooth expand/collapse animation
  • Chevron rotates when open
  • Keyboard: Enter/Space on the header toggles it
  • aria-expanded and aria-controls wired up

Concepts: event delegation · max-height transition · aria-expanded · state flags
accordion-vanilla.why:
• Track open ids in a Set. single mode: opening id X sets the set to {X}; multiple: toggles membership.
  • For animation: set max-height from scrollHeight (panel.scrollHeight + "px") then to 0. JS measures it; CSS transitions.

tabs-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Tabs with Keyboard Navigation
tabs-vanilla.what:
Build a Tabs component in vanilla JS: a tab list and panels. Support mouse clicks AND full keyboard nav: Left/Right arrows move focus (roving tabindex), Home/End jump, Enter/Space activates. Wire up ARIA roles: tablist, tab, tabpanel, aria-selected.

Requirements

  • Clicking a tab shows its panel and hides others
  • Left/Right arrows move between tabs (roving tabindex)
  • Home/End go to first/last tab
  • Enter/Space activates the focused tab
  • Only the active tab is in the tab order
  • aria-selected, aria-controls, role="tablist"/"tab"/"tabpanel"
  • Tab panel content updates without reload

Concepts: roving tabindex · ARIA tabs pattern · keyboard events · panel switching
tabs-vanilla.why:
• Roving tabindex: all tabs are tabindex="-1" except the active one (tabindex="0"). Arrow keys move the visual focus and update which is tabindex="0".
  • Panels: render all in the DOM, toggle hidden via the hidden attribute. aria-selected must live on the tab button.

modal-vanilla.desc: Focus trap, scroll lock, Escape handling — the hardest "easy" widget without React's portal.
modal-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Modal with Focus Trap (no portal)
modal-vanilla.what:
Build a Modal dialog in vanilla JS (no React, no portal): open on button click, overlay + centered dialog, close on Escape, on overlay click, and on the X button. Trap focus inside while open, restore focus to the trigger on close, and lock body scroll.

Requirements

  • Open/close with a smooth fade
  • Close via Escape, overlay click, and X button
  • Focus moves into the dialog on open
  • Tab/Shift+Tab cycle inside the dialog (focus trap)
  • Focus restored to the trigger button on close
  • body scroll locked while open (overflow:hidden)
  • role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby

Concepts: focus trap · event listeners · overflow lock · ARIA dialog
modal-vanilla.why:
• Focus trap: keydown listener — if e.key === "Tab", collect focusable elements in the dialog, wrap index at the ends. Save document.activeElement before opening.
  • Escape: document keydown listener, remove all listeners on close to avoid leaks. Overlay click: check e.target === overlay.

star-rating-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Star Rating (event delegation)
star-rating-vanilla.what:
Build a star rating widget: 5 stars, hover highlights up to the hovered star, click sets the rating, moving the mouse out restores the chosen rating. Support keyboard (arrow keys change the value) and a reset. Render from JS.

Requirements

  • Renders 5 interactive stars
  • Hover previews the rating without committing
  • Click commits the rating
  • Mouse leave restores the committed rating
  • Keyboard: Arrow keys adjust, Enter commits
  • Programmatic API: setRating(n) / getRating()
  • Star glyphs vs filled state switch smoothly

Concepts: event delegation · mouseover/mouseout · keydown · re-render
star-rating-vanilla.why:
• Put one listener on the container. e.target.closest(".star") gives the index — set data-rating on each star.
  • Keep state = {hovered, value}. render() redraws star classes: filled when i <= (hovered || value).

stopwatch-vanilla.desc: setInterval drift and lap recording — timing precision under the microscope.
stopwatch-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Stopwatch with Laps
stopwatch-vanilla.what:
Build a stopwatch in vanilla JS: Start/Pause/Reset buttons, an elapsed time display (MM:SS.cs), and a lap list that records each split with its cumulative time and the lap delta. Use a timestamp-based timer so it never drifts.

Requirements

  • Start/Pause/Reset controls
  • Display updates with centisecond precision
  • Uses timestamps (performance.now()) not interval counting
  • Lap button records cumulative time + lap delta
  • Laps render as a scrollable list (newest first)
  • Reset clears laps and display
  • Formatting: MM:SS.cc

Concepts: setInterval vs timestamps · performance.now() · state machine · DOM list rendering
stopwatch-vanilla.why:
• Drift fix: store startTime on start; each tick compute elapsed = now - startTime - accumulated. Interval only drives the re-render at ~50ms.
  • Lap delta = current elapsed - last lap elapsed. Store laps as [{cum, delta}]. Render with a fragment and prepend.

countdown-vanilla.desc: A ring that drains as time passes — SVG stroke-dashoffset meets the timer pattern.
countdown-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Countdown Timer with Progress Ring
countdown-vanilla.what:
Build a countdown timer with an SVG progress ring: set minutes/seconds, start/pause/reset, and a ring whose circumference visibly drains. Flash the display red and fire an alarm state in the last 10 seconds. Optional preset buttons (1/5/10 min).

Requirements

  • Set target duration (minutes + seconds inputs)
  • Start/Pause/Reset
  • SVG ring drains proportionally as time passes
  • Display shows remaining time MM:SS
  • Last 10s: number turns red / pulses
  • At zero: stops, shows 00:00 and a visual alarm
  • Runs from a deadline timestamp, not decrement counting

Concepts: SVG stroke-dashoffset · deadline timestamps · requestAnimationFrame/setInterval · state machine
countdown-vanilla.why:
• Ring: a circle with stroke-dasharray = C (circumference) and stroke-dashoffset = C * (1 - remaining/total). Transition the offset for smoothness.
  • Deadline: store end = Date.now() + remainingMs. On each tick compute remainingMs = end - Date.now() — immune to setInterval drift and throttling.

form-validation-vanilla.desc: Real-time validation with error messages and a11y — the form round nobody practices.
form-validation-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Inline Form Validation
form-validation-vanilla.what:
Build a form (name, email, password, confirm password) with vanilla JS validation: validate on blur and on submit, show inline error messages, mark invalid fields with an error style and aria-invalid, focus the first invalid field on submit, and clear the error as the user types.

Requirements

  • Validates: name non-empty, email regex, password >= 8 chars with a number, confirm matches
  • Errors show inline under each field
  • Validate on blur and on submit
  • Fields get .error class + aria-invalid=true
  • On submit: focus first invalid field, don't send
  • Error clears as the user fixes the input
  • Success state shows a message; no framework

Concepts: FormData · regex validation · blur/submit/input events · aria-invalid
form-validation-vanilla.why:
• Map each field to a validator fn returning an error string or "". A single validateField(el) function reads the map.
  • On submit, run all validators, collect invalid fields, focus the first, and e.preventDefault(). For UX: validate a field only after it has been touched (blurred once).

carousel-vanilla.desc: Infinite looping, dots, swipe, and auto-play — the widget that is 90% edge cases.
carousel-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Image Carousel (vanilla)
carousel-vanilla.what:
Build an image carousel in vanilla JS: prev/next arrows, dot indicators, auto-play with pause-on-hover, and a wrapping loop (after the last slide comes the first). Support touch swipe on mobile. No framework.

Requirements

  • Prev/next arrows advance/wrap around
  • Dot indicators reflect and jump to a slide
  • Auto-play every 3s, stops on hover/focus, resumes on leave
  • Swipe left/right on touch devices
  • Animated slide transition (translateX)
  • Slide counter or aria-live region for a11y
  • Resizes gracefully (no layout jump)

Concepts: translateX transforms · setInterval auto-play · touch events · indices with modulo

infinite-scroll-vanilla.desc: A sentinel element + IntersectionObserver loads the next page — async UX fundamentals.
infinite-scroll-vanilla.q: How would you solve this problem? Infinite Scroll (IntersectionObserver)
infinite-scroll-vanilla.what:
Build an infinite scroll list in vanilla JS: start with 20 items, when the user scrolls to the sentinel element, fetch/render the next 20 with a loading spinner, debounced so it doesn't double-fire. Show "no more" at the end. Items can come from a mock async source.

Requirements

  • Renders initial batch of items
  • Loading more triggers when sentinel enters viewport
  • Uses IntersectionObserver (not scroll math)
  • Spinner shows while loading; no duplicate loads
  • Stops loading at "no more items"
  • New items append without layout thrash
  • Optionally dedupe with requestAnimationFrame

Concepts: IntersectionObserver · async data source · sentinel pattern · lazy rendering
infinite-scroll-vanilla.why:
• Place an empty div at the list bottom. observer.observe(sentinel). In the callback, if isIntersecting and not loading, load more.
  • Guard: a loading flag checked before fetch and reset in finally. When the source is exhausted, unobserve the sentinel.

autocomplete-vanilla.desc: The canonical frontend problem without React: async, debounce, keyboard nav, highlight.
autocomplete-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Autocomplete (debounce + keyboard)
autocomplete-vanilla.what:
Build a production-quality autocomplete in vanilla JS: a text input, debounced suggestions (300ms) from a mock async API, a dropdown filtered on the client, Up/Down/Enter/Escape keyboard navigation, and highlighted matching substrings. Handle loading and empty states.

Requirements

  • Debounce the suggestion request by 300ms
  • Loading indicator while awaiting results
  • Keyboard: Up/Down move highlight, Enter selects, Escape closes
  • Matches highlight inside each suggestion
  • Click selects a suggestion
  • Empty results state shown
  • Caches results by query string

Concepts: debounce · async/await · keyboard navigation · marking matches
autocomplete-vanilla.why:
• Debounce: clearTimeout/setTimeout in the input's "input" handler. Cache: a Map.
  • Highlight: for each suggestion, find the query index and wrap the match in (or a span.highlight). Escape HTML from the server text first.

pagination-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Client-side Pagination
pagination-vanilla.what:
Build a pagination control in vanilla JS for a fixed data array: N items per page, prev/next, page-number buttons with a window (current page in the middle, ellipses at the edges), and a "Showing X–Y of Z" line. Keep the list rendered from the current slice.

Requirements

  • Configurable page size (e.g. 10)
  • Prev/Next buttons (disabled at the ends)
  • Page-number buttons with a sliding window + ellipses
  • Active page highlighted and aria-current="page"
  • "Showing X–Y of Z" caption updates
  • Clicking a number re-renders only the list + controls
  • Handles edge: fewer items than one page

Concepts: slice() pagination · windowed page lists · ellipsis logic · re-render
pagination-vanilla.why:
• currentSlice = data.slice((page-1)*size, page*size). Re-render list + caption on every page change.
  • Page window: pages = max 7 numbers. Show 1 … leftWindow … current … rightWindow … last with "…" when gaps exist. Build the array conditionally.

traffic-light-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Traffic Light State Machine
traffic-light-vanilla.what:
Build a traffic light with vanilla JS: three circles (red/amber/green). A finite state machine cycles them automatically (red 4s → amber 1s → green 3s → amber 1s → red). Clicking the light advances one state manually for testing.

Requirements

  • Three lamp circles, one active at a time
  • Automatic cycle with per-state durations
  • Manual advance on click (moves to next state)
  • Model as an explicit state machine, not scattered if/else
  • Start immediately on load
  • Clear transition between states

Concepts: state machines · setTimeout chains · state -> view mapping · event-driven updates
traffic-light-vanilla.why:
• Define states = [{id:"red",next:"amber",ms:4000}, ...]. A setState(s) renders the light and schedules setTimeout for the next state.
  • Keep the interval/timer handle so a manual click can clearTimeout and jump. Manual advance uses the same next pointer.

grid-light-vanilla.desc: A classic Flipkart machine coding round — click a cell, fill the diagonal, then reset in order.
grid-light-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Grid Light (Flipkart round)
grid-light-vanilla.what:
Build a Grid Light (Flipkart-style): a 3x3 grid. Clicking a cell turns it on along with its diagonal cells. When all 9 cells are on, they turn off one-by-one in the order they were activated. Track activation order explicitly.

Requirements

  • 3x3 grid rendered from JS
  • Clicking a cell lights it + its diagonal cells
  • Cells toggle based on the diagonal rule, not independently
  • When all cells are on, they turn off sequentially in activation order
  • Lighting respects the diagonal dependency
  • Restarts cleanly after the reset sequence

Concepts: state tracking · activation order · grid modeling · async timing
grid-light-vanilla.why:
• Model cells as [[0,0],[1,1],[2,2]] diagonal mapping. cell(i,j) is on if any clicked cell on its diagonal lit it — derive state from clicked set, don't mutate flags.
  • For the reset: keep an order[] of clicked cells. When full, setTimeout chain turning off in order with a small delay.

tic-tac-toe-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Tic-Tac-Toe with History (vanilla)
tic-tac-toe-vanilla.what:
Build Tic-Tac-Toe in vanilla JS: two players alternate X/O, win detection for rows/columns/diagonals, a draw state, a status line, and a move history that lets you jump back to any earlier board state. No framework.

Requirements

  • Clicking an empty cell places the current player's mark
  • Turn alternates X/O
  • Wins detected for 3 rows, 3 columns, 2 diagonals
  • Draw detected when board full with no winner
  • Status line shows whose turn / result
  • Move history: list of moves; clicking jumps to that state
  • Past states immutable (no mutation bugs)

Concepts: game state modeling · win detection · immutable snapshots · history navigation
tic-tac-toe-vanilla.why:
• Board as an array of 9. Win check: compare against 8 winning triples with Array.every. Each move pushes a copy of the board into history.
  • History jump: slice the history array and rebuild the board from the chosen index — never mutate past boards in place.

memory-game-vanilla.q: How would you solve this problem? Memory Match Game
memory-game-vanilla.why:
• Fisher-Yates: for i from n-1 down to 1, swap with random index 0..i. Store cards as {id, value}.
  • State: flipped = up to 2 card ids + matched Set. On second flip, compare values; if equal add to matched, else setTimeout 800ms to flip both back and lock clicks during the wait.

calculator-vanilla.desc: Operator precedence, chained math, and display state — the trickiest "simple" UI.
calculator-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Calculator
calculator-vanilla.what:
Build a calculator in vanilla JS: digits 0-9, decimal point, + - × ÷, clear, and equals. Support chained operations (2 + 3 × 4 = 14) using proper operator precedence, and prevent double-operators/leading-zeros. Keyboard input support (digits and operators).

Requirements

  • Digit and decimal input with sane limits
  • +, -, ×, ÷ with precedence (×/÷ before +-)
  • Chained evaluation, e.g. 2 + 3 × 4 = 14
  • Equals computes and continues from the result
  • Clear resets; backspace deletes last digit
  • Handles divide-by-zero gracefully
  • Keyboard support for digits/operators/Enter

Concepts: tokenization · operator precedence · display state · keyboard events
calculator-vanilla.why:
• Build the expression as tokens and evaluate with shunting-yard or two-pass: first ×/÷, then +- (left to right).
  • Keep display as the current number string; build expression string for evaluation. Guard: leading "." -> "0.", no "..", no trailing operator on equals.

weather-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Weather App (fetch + states)
weather-vanilla.why:
• State machine: {status: idle|loading|success|error|notfound, data}. render() switches on status — one render path per state.
  • Mock API: a function returning a Promise that resolves after a delay with a fake forecast map keyed by city. Error = the same function rejecting on unknown city after a debounce.

file-upload-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Drag & Drop File Upload
file-upload-vanilla.what:
Build a file upload zone in vanilla JS: a drop area (drag-over highlights it), file input fallback, a file list with name/size, image previews, and simulated upload progress bars with cancel. Restrict to images (or accept filter).

Requirements

  • Click-to-browse opens the file picker
  • Drag-over highlights the drop zone
  • Drop adds files to the list (no duplicates)
  • Image previews rendered via URL.createObjectURL
  • Each file shows name, size, and a progress bar
  • Simulated upload with progress + cancel
  • Invalid type shows an error toast

Concepts: dragenter/dragover/drop · URL.createObjectURL · progress simulation · file validation
file-upload-vanilla.why:
• Prevent default on dragover/drop or the browser navigates away. Track a drag counter to avoid flicker on child enter/leave.
  • Progress: setInterval advancing 0->100 per file, or a slow-approach curve (p += (100-p)*0.1). Cancel = clearInterval + mark file failed.

drag-drop-vanilla.desc: HTML5 DnD with live reordering — the interview favorite that catches everyone.
drag-drop-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Drag & Drop Reorder / Kanban
drag-drop-vanilla.what:
Build a drag-and-drop list (or single-column kanban) in vanilla JS: drag items to reorder them, with a live insertion indicator (ghost) showing where the item will land. Support dragstart/dragover/drop; the list re-renders from state after every drop.

Requirements

  • Drag an item to reorder it within the list
  • Live visual insertion point while dragging
  • Drop commits the new order (state updates)
  • Only the dragged item moves (not a copy)
  • Drag handle or full-row draggable
  • Keyboard alternative for reordering (bonus)
  • Works with mouse only (touch is bonus)

Concepts: dragstart/dragover/drop · dragenter index math · state-based re-render · visual feedback
drag-drop-vanilla.why:
• On dragover, compute the target index from the list items' bounding boxes and show a ghost line before/after that item.
  • On drop: splice the dragged item out of state and back in at the ghost index, then re-render the list. The source item keeps class dragging during the drag.

toast-vanilla.desc: A queue + auto-dismiss + stacking — the tiny system that separates widget coders.
toast-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Toast Notification System
toast-vanilla.what:
Build a toast notification system in vanilla JS: a toast(message, type) API (success/info/error/warning), toasts stack in the top-right, auto-dismiss after 4s with a manual close button, and multiple toasts don't overlap. Cap the visible stack (e.g. max 5).

Requirements

  • toast(message, type) exposes the public API
  • Four types with distinct colors/icons
  • Auto-dismiss after 4s with countdown (bonus)
  • Manual close button
  • Toasts stack cleanly (top-right container)
  • Max 5 visible; oldest is removed beyond that
  • A11y: role="status"/"alert" for each toast

Concepts: event emitter / pub-sub · DOM creation · timers · container pattern
toast-vanilla.why:
• Create one container div on init (fixed, top-right). Each toast is a div appended with a class per type.
  • Auto-dismiss: setTimeout(remove, 4000). For max N, when length > 5 remove the first child. Close button removes + clears its timer.

chips-input-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Chips / Tags Input
chips-input-vanilla.what:
Build a chips (tags) input in vanilla JS: type a tag, press Enter (or comma) to add it as a chip; chips have an × to remove; pressing Backspace on an empty input removes the last chip; duplicates are rejected with a shake/error. Provide a value getter for the chips.

Requirements

  • Enter or comma commits the typed value as a chip
  • Chips render with a remove (×) button
  • Backspace on empty input removes the last chip
  • Duplicate values rejected with an error flash
  • Leading/trailing whitespace trimmed
  • Input cleared after committing a chip
  • Chips accessible: getChips() returns the array

Concepts: keydown handling · deduplication · chip removal · input width auto-grow
chips-input-vanilla.why:
• Handle keydown on the input: Enter/comma -> commit; Backspace with value=="" -> remove last chip; Escape -> clear.
  • Auto-grow the input: set its width to scrollWidth (or a hidden span mirror) so the text never overflows the pill row.

snake-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Snake on Canvas
snake-vanilla.what:
Build Snake on a <canvas> with vanilla JS: a grid-based snake that moves on a fixed tick, grows when it eats food, wraps or dies on walls (your choice — call it out), dies on self-collision, and a score/restart. Arrow/WASD input with direction buffering so a fast turn isn't lost.

Requirements

  • Snake moves on a fixed interval (grid tick)
  • Arrow keys + WASD control direction
  • Direction can't reverse into itself
  • Input buffering: two rapid turns in one tick both register
  • Food spawns randomly on empty cells
  • Eating grows the snake and increments score
  • Self-collision ends the game; restart button
  • Rendered on canvas with clear frame loop

Concepts: game loop · linked-list / queue body model · input buffering · canvas rendering
snake-vanilla.why:
• Model the snake as a queue (head at front). Move = unshift(newHead), pop tail (unless growing). Body rendering = draw each cell rect.
  • Input buffer: push direction changes to an array; on each tick shift one and apply only if not the reverse of the current direction.

minesweeper-vanilla.desc: Flood-fill reveal, adjacency counting, and chording — the Google hard favorite.
minesweeper-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Minesweeper (flood fill)
minesweeper-vanilla.what:
Build Minesweeper in vanilla JS: a 9x9 board with 10 mines, first-click-safe, reveal cells with an adjacent-mine count, flood-fill open zero cells (BFS/DFS), right-click to flag, a win condition (all non-mine cells revealed) and a loss on mine click. Timer + reset.

Requirements

  • 9x9 grid, 10 mines placed randomly
  • First click never hits a mine (move it)
  • Revealing a 0 opens its whole region (flood fill)
  • Numbers show adjacent mine counts
  • Right-click flags/unflags a cell (counter shown)
  • Clicking a mine reveals all and ends the game
  • Win detected when every non-mine cell is revealed
  • Reset reshuffles and restarts

Concepts: flood fill (BFS) · adjacency counting · game state · right-click handling
minesweeper-vanilla.why:
• Model as a 2D array of cell objects {mine, revealed, flagged, adj}. BFS stack: push neighbors of revealed 0-cells within bounds, skipping visited.
  • Place mines after the first click using a candidate list excluding the clicked cell + its neighbors. adjacency = count mines among the 8 neighbors.

game-2048-vanilla.desc: Tile merging, sliding, and spawn logic — the ultimate grid state-machine round.
game-2048-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? 2048 Game
game-2048-vanilla.what:
Build the 2048 game in vanilla JS: a 4x4 grid, arrow keys slide all tiles in that direction, equal adjacent tiles merge (each tile merges once per move), a random 2/4 spawns after each valid move, score tracks merged values, and the game ends when no moves remain (or 2048 is reached).

Requirements

  • Arrow keys slide + merge all tiles
  • A tile merges at most once per move
  • Random 2 (90%) or 4 (10%) spawns after a valid move
  • No-move-on-this-direction leaves the board unchanged
  • Score increments by merged values
  • Win banner at 2048 (continue optional)
  • Game-over detection: board full and no merges possible
  • Animated slide/merge feel (CSS transitions)

Concepts: grid transformation · merge logic · spawn logic · valid-move detection
game-2048-vanilla.why:
• Slide-left algorithm: per row, compress (remove zeros), merge adjacent equals once, re-compress. Rotate the board 4 times to reuse it for all directions.
  • Valid move = any cell changed. Copy board before the attempt (JSON/structured clone) to compare. Possible move check: any empty cell OR any adjacent equal pair.

canvas-drawing-vanilla.q: How would you solve this problem? Drawing Board with Undo/Redo
canvas-drawing-vanilla.what:
Build a drawing board on canvas: draw freehand with the mouse or pen (pointer events), pick color and stroke width, undo/redo stroke-by-stroke, and clear. Snapshots are stored as stroke arrays (not pixel images) so undo is cheap and lossless.

Requirements

  • Freehand drawing via pointer events (down/move/up)
  • Color and stroke-width pickers apply live
  • Undo removes the last stroke; redo restores it
  • Clear wipes the board
  • Stroke model: [{points, color, width}]
  • High-DPI aware: canvas sized to devicePixelRatio
  • Touch support (pointer events unify mouse + touch)

Concepts: Pointer Events · stroke vectorization · undo/redo stacks · canvas DPI scaling

virtual-list-vanilla.desc: Render 100,000 rows as ~10 DOM nodes — the performance round everyone flubs.
virtual-list-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Virtual Scrolling List
virtual-list-vanilla.what:
Build a virtual scrolling list in vanilla JS: render only the visible window of a large array (e.g. 100,000 rows) inside a fixed-height scroll container. On scroll, compute the visible range, render only those rows with absolute/translateY positioning, and keep a small buffer. Variable row heights optional (bonus).

Requirements

  • Fixed-height scroll container
  • Renders only visible rows + buffer (e.g. 5 each side)
  • Row positions via translateY, not top (no layout thrash)
  • Handles 100k+ rows without lag
  • Scroll position stable when jumping to a row
  • Click on a row fires a callback with the row index
  • Resize/row-height change re-measures

Concepts: virtualization · scroll events + rAF throttling · translateY positioning · window/range math

data-table-vanilla.desc: Sorting, filtering, and row selection — the most common dashboard component.
data-table-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Sortable / Filterable Data Table

chat-vanilla.desc: A WebSocket client, message list, and reconnect logic — real-time from the raw API.
chat-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? WebSocket Chat UI (vanilla)
chat-vanilla.what:
Build a chat UI in vanilla JS talking to a WebSocket endpoint: send messages, render incoming messages (own vs other with different alignment), show typing indicator and online status, auto-scroll to the latest, and reconnect with backoff on disconnect. Include a message input with Enter to send.

Requirements

  • Connects to a WebSocket (ws:// or a mock)
  • Send message via input + Enter/button
  • Renders own vs peer messages with alignment
  • Auto-scrolls to newest unless user scrolled up
  • Online/disconnected status indicator
  • Reconnect with exponential backoff
  • Typing indicator (bonus)
  • Handles connection error gracefully

Concepts: WebSocket API · reconnect backoff · message rendering · scroll anchoring
chat-vanilla.why:
• Socket events: onopen/onmessage/onclose/onerror. Track connection state in a status banner. Reconnect: schedule ws = new WebSocket(url) with increasing delay, reset on open.
  • Scroll anchoring: if user is near the bottom (scrollTop near max) auto-scroll after append; otherwise show a "new message" jump chip.

reactive-framework-vanilla.desc: Reactive state -> DOM updates — the tiny framework behind Vue/Solid, built by hand.
reactive-framework-vanilla.q: How would you solve this problem? Mini Reactive DOM Framework

dom-diff-vanilla.desc: createElement, mount, and patch — build the React reconciliation core in vanilla.
dom-diff-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Virtual DOM Diff (vanilla)

spreadsheet-vanilla.desc: A grid of cells, formula evaluation, and dependency recalculation — the wildcard round.
spreadsheet-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Spreadsheet Grid with Formulas
spreadsheet-vanilla.why:
• Parse references with a regex for ([A-J])(d+). Build a dependency graph cell -> dependents. On edit, recompute affected cells in topological order.
  • Eval safely: build the expression by substituting referenced cell values, then evaluate with new Function(...)? Safer: write a tiny recursive-descent evaluator handling + - * / and SUM/AVG over ranges.

file-explorer-vanilla.desc: A recursive folder tree with expand/collapse, CRUD, and rename — recursion in the DOM.
file-explorer-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? File Explorer (Folder Tree)
file-explorer-vanilla.what:
Build a file explorer in vanilla JS from a nested {name, type: 'folder'|'file', children?} tree: render the hierarchy recursively, folders expand/collapse with an arrow, files select on click, and the toolbar supports new folder / new file / rename / delete on the selected node. Empty folders, deep nesting, and indentation guides.

Requirements

  • Renders the full tree recursively (folder > file nesting)
  • Folder arrow toggles expand/collapse; state persists
  • Click selects a node (highlight + toolbar enabled)
  • New folder / new file creates a child under the selected folder
  • Rename edits the node name inline (Enter/Escape)
  • Delete removes the node and its whole subtree
  • Folder name length/path-depth edge cases handled
  • Indentation guides render for each depth level

Concepts: recursive rendering · tree CRUD · immutable tree updates · event delegation
file-explorer-vanilla.why:
• Model state as a single tree object; all operations return a new tree (map over children recursively). Render one recursive function renderNode(node, depth) and compose containers.
  • Delegation: one click listener reads data-id, resolves the node path, then rerenders. Paths: keep a path array (indices) in data-path so operations can rebuild the tree immutably.

nested-comments-vanilla.desc: Recursive comment threads with reply, delete, and vote — the infinite-nesting classic.
nested-comments-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Nested Comments (Reddit-style)
nested-comments-vanilla.what:
Build nested comments in vanilla JS: a top-level comment box, replies nest recursively to any depth, each comment has reply / upvote-downvote / delete (with a confirm). Reply opens an inline editor, and every comment shows an author, relative time, and score. A collapse toggle hides a comment and all of its children.

Requirements

  • Comments render as a recursive thread tree
  • Reply adds a child comment to any depth
  • Inline reply editor (textarea + post/cancel)
  • Upvote/downvote increments a score (one vote per comment)
  • Delete removes the comment and all descendants
  • Collapse toggle hides a comment and its subtree
  • Authors + relative timestamps rendered
  • No framework: pure DOM building + event delegation

Concepts: recursive rendering · tree state updates · event delegation · voting state
nested-comments-vanilla.why:
• Comment node = {id, author, text, time, score, children[]}. renderThread(comment) returns the DOM for that subtree; rerender the whole thread on every mutation (data is small).
  • Reply: keep editingCommentId in state; the editor renders inline under that node. Deleting = filter node out recursively via map over children.

json-tree-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? JSON Tree Viewer
json-tree-vanilla.what:
Build a JSON tree viewer in vanilla JS: paste any JSON (or load a sample) and render it as an indented, collapsible tree — objects and arrays expand/collapse with a toggle, primitives are color-coded (string green, number blue, boolean purple, null gray), keys are clickable to copy the path, and a search box highlights + jumps to matching keys.

Requirements

  • Parses JSON input (error state for invalid)
  • Objects and arrays render with expand/collapse toggles
  • Type-based color coding for primitives
  • Keys copy their JSONPath on click (e.g. a.b[0].c)
  • Search highlights matching keys and jumps to first
  • Large inputs stay responsive (lazy render children)
  • Empty object/array shown inline as {} / []

Concepts: recursive rendering · mixed-type introspection · JSONPath · lazy expansion

checkbox-tree-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Cascading Checkbox Tree
checkbox-tree-vanilla.what:
Build a cascading checkbox tree in vanilla JS from a nested permissions list (e.g. Settings > Notifications > Email): checking a parent checks all descendants, unchecking clears all, a partially-checked parent renders an indeterminate box, and any manual child change recomputes ancestors. A footer shows the total selected / total count.

Requirements

  • Renders a nested checkbox list recursively
  • Checking a parent checks its entire subtree
  • Unchecking a parent unchecks its entire subtree
  • Parent with some checked children shows indeterminate state
  • Manual child toggle recomputes all ancestors
  • Leaf count + selected count shown in the footer
  • Checkbox + label click both toggle the node

Concepts: recursive state propagation · indeterminate state · derived state · tree traversal

directory-size-vanilla.desc: Recursive size aggregation over a fake filesystem — the math behind disk-usage tools.
directory-size-vanilla.q: How will you solve this problem? Directory Size Calculator
directory-size-vanilla.what:
Build a directory size calculator in vanilla JS: a fake file tree where files carry byte sizes and folders aggregate their subtree total, rendered with each node's size right-aligned. Expand/collapse folders, sort children by size desc, and a 'calculate all' scan that animates folder totals filling in (walking the tree recursively with a delay).

Requirements

  • File tree with per-file sizes and folders aggregating subtrees
  • Size shown right-aligned per row, formatted (B/KB/MB)
  • Expand/collapse folders
  • Sort children by size descending (toggle)
  • Scan animation: folder totals fill in bottom-up
  • Recursive aggregation computes totals once and caches
  • Large trees: total displayed at the root

Concepts: recursive aggregation · post-order traversal · size formatting · animation timing
directory-size-vanilla.why:
• A folder's size = sum of children, computed post-order: size(node) = files sum + folders.map(size). Cache results in a Map so toggling sort doesn't recompute.
  • For the scan animation, flatten the post-order sequence into a list, then reveal each folder's total on a setTimeout/setInterval tick (or rAF).

todo-app.desc: The "Hello World" of machine coding. But nailing the edge cases sets you apart.
todo-app.q: How will you solve this problem? Todo App with Filters

accordion.q: How will you solve this problem? Accordion Component
accordion.why:
• Single mode: store openId (one value). Multiple mode: store Set of openIds. Render conditionally based on whether item.id is in the open set.
  • For smooth height: use max-height transition from 0 to max-content. Or use a ref to measure content height and animate to it.

modal.desc: Looks simple. The gotchas (focus trap, scroll lock, portal) reveal your seniority.
modal.q: How will you solve this problem? Modal / Dialog Component
modal.what:
Build a reusable Modal component. It should: render in a portal, trap focus inside, close on backdrop click and ESC key, lock body scroll when open, and support a header/footer/body layout.

Requirements

  • Render into document.body via createPortal
  • Close on backdrop click (not on modal content click)
  • Close on ESC keydown
  • Lock body scroll (overflow: hidden) while open
  • Focus trap: Tab cycles only inside modal
  • First focusable element receives focus on open
  • Restore focus to trigger element on close

Concepts: useEffect · createPortal · refs · keyboard events · focus management
modal.why:
• Use useRef to store the element that had focus before modal opened. On close, call storedRef.current.focus().
  • Focus trap: on keydown Tab, check if focused element is the last focusable. If yes, move to first. Query all focusable elements inside the modal.

star-rating.q: How will you solve this problem? Star Rating Component
star-rating.what:
Build a StarRating component with: controlled rating, hover preview, half-star support, readonly mode, and custom size/color. Fire onChange(rating) callback.

Requirements

  • Render N stars (default 5, configurable)
  • Hover over a star previews that rating
  • Click sets the rating (fires onChange)
  • Readonly mode: no interaction
  • Half-star: hovering left half of star = x.5 rating
  • ARIA: role="radiogroup", each star role="radio" with aria-checked

Concepts: useState · mouse events · controlled components · ARIA · CSS

tabs.q: How will you solve this problem? Tabs Component
tabs.what:
Build a Tabs component accepting [{id, label, content}]. Support: keyboard navigation (arrow keys), lazy loading panels, controlled and uncontrolled modes, and vertical/horizontal orientation.

Requirements

  • Click tab to show panel
  • Arrow Left/Right (horizontal) or Up/Down (vertical) to navigate
  • Home/End keys jump to first/last tab
  • Lazy: only render panel content when tab has been active (mount once, keep in DOM)
  • ARIA: role="tablist", role="tab", role="tabpanel", aria-selected

Concepts: useState · keyboard events · ARIA · lazy rendering · controlled components
tabs.why:
• For lazy rendering: track a Set of "everActivated" tab ids. Only render panel if id is in the set. Display with visibility/hidden instead of unmounting.
  • For keyboard: keep a ref to all tab elements. On arrow key, focus the adjacent tab using tabRef[newIndex].focus().

countdown.q: How will you solve this problem? Countdown Timer
countdown.why:
• Use setInterval inside useEffect. Clear it on pause/unmount. Store remaining time in state. On each tick, decrement and check for zero.
  • For the SVG ring: circumference = 2*π*r. stroke-dashoffset = circumference * (1 - progress). Animate with CSS transition.

pagination.q: How will you solve this problem? Pagination Component

otp-input.q: How will you solve this problem? OTP Input Component

searchable-dropdown.q: How will you solve this problem? Searchable Dropdown
searchable-dropdown.why:
• Use a ref on the container div for outside click detection. useEffect: document.addEventListener("mousedown", handler). Check if ref.current.contains(event.target).
  • For text highlighting: split option label by the search term and wrap matching parts in .

progress-bar.desc: Clamping, threshold colors, and indeterminate mode - the small details interviewers check.
progress-bar.q: How will you solve this problem? Progress Bar Component
progress-bar.what:
Build a ProgressBar component with props value, max (default 100), and color. Clamp value to [0, max]. Support threshold-based color zones and an indeterminate animation mode.

Requirements

  • value clamped between 0 and max (no negative or overflowing width)
